From metacells to programs: the SuperCell + mcRigor workflow

metacells_to_programs.Rmd

This article runs the full cellprograms pipeline downstream of metacell construction. The starting point is a single-cell Seurat object; metacells are built with the default SuperCell 2.0 + mcRigor backend (pure R — no Python; see “Metacells: SuperCell (default) and SEACells” for construction details and the benchmark behind the default), and the metacell counts then feed program discovery, stability assessment, coordinated multicellular program (CMP) detection, sharing assessment, and cell-level projection.

The fixture plants known truth so every downstream call can be checked: two cell types across 24 donors, each type with a private program (constant across donors) and a coordinated program whose donor activities are correlated across the two cell types.

Simulate a single-cell dataset with planted programs

24 donors x two cell types x 60 cells, 800 genes. Genes 1:40 are a T-cell-private marker block; genes 81:120 a B-cell-private block; genes 41:80 form the coordinated block, expressed in both cell types with a donor activity gradient (lambda rising from 0.5 to 8.5 across donors) that is shared across types — the planted CMP. Everything else is background Poisson noise.

library(cellprograms)
set.seed(7)

n_donor <- 24; n_cell <- 60; n_gene <- 800
types <- c("Tcells", "Bcells")
donors <- paste0("d", seq_len(n_donor))
a_grad <- seq_len(n_donor)                # planted donor activity gradient

groups <- unlist(lapply(donors, function(d) paste0(d, "_", rep(types, each = n_cell))),
                 use.names = FALSE)
lam <- matrix(0.5, nrow = n_gene, ncol = length(groups))
for (d in seq_len(n_donor)) {
  for (t in seq_along(types)) {
    cols <- which(groups == paste0(donors[d], "_", types[t]))
    private <- if (types[t] == "Tcells") 1:40 else 81:120
    lam[private, cols] <- 8                          # private block, constant
    lam[41:80, cols] <- 0.5 + 8 * (d - 1) / (n_donor - 1)  # coordinated gradient
  }
}
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(rpois(n_gene * length(groups), as.vector(lam)),
                         nrow = n_gene, ncol = length(groups), sparse = TRUE)
rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", seq_len(n_gene))
colnames(counts) <- paste0("cell", seq_len(length(groups)))

meta <- data.frame(
  donor = sub("_.*", "", groups),
  celltype = sub(".*_", "", groups),
  row.names = colnames(counts)
)

Build metacells (SuperCell 2.0 + mcRigor)

Metacells are built per donor x cell type so they never cross either variable. cells_per_metacell = 15 turns each 60-cell group into ~4 metacells; mcRigor QC runs on every group.

obj <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts, meta.data = meta)
obj <- Seurat::NormalizeData(obj, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(obj, nfeatures = 200, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::ScaleData(obj, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::RunPCA(obj, npcs = 10, verbose = FALSE)

obj <- MetacellsByGroupsSuperCell(obj,
                                  group.by = c("donor", "celltype"),
                                  cells_per_metacell = 15,
                                  min_cells = 50,
                                  n_top_genes = 200,
                                  n_pc = 10,
                                  mcrigor_args = list(Nrep = 5),
                                  seed = 7, verbose = FALSE)
res <- GetMetacellSuperCell(obj)
mc <- res$metacell_object
ncol(mc)                          # total metacells
head(res$qc[, c("metacell", "mcDiv", "dubious")])

OptimizeGammaSuperCell() can replace the fixed cells_per_metacell when you want the granularity chosen by the mcRigor score (see the metacells article); the downstream workflow is identical either way.

Metacell counts to donor pseudobulk

With mode = "sum" (the default), summing metacell counts within donor x cell type reproduces the donor pseudobulk exactly — the metacell layer is lossless at the donor level and simply denoises the cells the pseudobulk is built from. We log-normalize the aggregated counts with the standard log1p(count / library size x 10^4) recipe and declare the fit’s measurement units as "logcounts" (this is what later lets us project the programs back onto single cells).

counts_mc <- SeuratObject::LayerData(mc[["RNA"]], layer = "counts")  # genes x metacells
mc_donor <- mc$donor                       # group columns are copied to the
mc_type <- mc$celltype                     # metacell object's metadata

pb <- lapply(types, function(t) {
  mcs <- colnames(mc)[mc_type == t]
  agg <- rowsum(t(as.matrix(counts_mc[, mcs, drop = FALSE])),
                group = mc_donor[mcs])              # donors x genes (counts)
  agg <- agg[donors, , drop = FALSE]
  lib <- rowSums(agg)
  out <- log1p(sweep(agg, 1, lib, "/") * 1e4)       # donors x genes (logcounts)
  rownames(out) <- donors   # same donor id across types: how CMP pairing
  out                       # knows which donors are shared
})
names(pb) <- types
lapply(pb, dim)

sample_metadata <- data.frame(
  observation_id = donors,
  planted_activity = a_grad
)
x <- as_cell_program_data(pb, sample_metadata = sample_metadata)

Fit and canonicalize programs

One empirical-Bayes matrix factorization per cell type; the coordinated block’s donor-varying activity and the private blocks’ constant activity should both be recovered as programs.

fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x, loading_prior = "point_laplace",
                             max_factors = 3, features = "variable",
                             n_variable_genes = 400,
                             feature_scale = "logcounts")
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)
program_summary(fit)[, c("cell_type", "n_programs", "R2", "elbo")]
top_genes(fit, "Tcells_1", n = 6)
top_genes(fit, "Bcells_1", n = 6)

The donor x program score matrix carries the planted gradient: the coordinated programs’ scores track the donor index, the private programs are flat.

Z <- program_scores(fit)
plot_program_scores(fit, annotation = "planted_activity")
plot_variance_explained(fit)

Stability

assess_program_stability() refits on donor subsamples and reports how often each program is recovered — the same guarantee as in the pseudobulk workflow, now on metacell-derived inputs.

fit <- assess_program_stability(fit, n_boot = 4, resample_frac = 0.7,
                                seed = 7, progress = FALSE)
fit$stability$per_program[, c("program_id", "recovery_freq")]

Coordinated multicellular programs

find_coordinated_programs() tests whether programs from different cell types co-vary across donors. The planted truth: the two programs of the coordinated block (one per type) share donor activity; the private programs do not.

cmp <- find_coordinated_programs(fit, n_perm = 99, seed = 7)
cmp
plot_cmp_network(cmp)

The coordinated-block pair is called; the private programs (constant donor activity, independent noise) are not. annotate_cmp_tf() / cmp_triage() add TF-footprint annotation and triage on real data (external CollecTRI download, not run here).

Shared vs specific programs

program_sharing() asks whether matched programs share their gene effects — here the coordinated block is literally the same genes in both types, so a shared call on the coordinated pair is the planted truth.

if (requireNamespace("mashr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  shr <- program_sharing(fit, n_perm = 99, seed = 7)
  shr$matches
  plot_sharing(shr)
}

Project programs back onto single cells

Because the fit declared feature_scale = "logcounts", the fitted programs can be projected onto the original single cells (project_programs_to_cells() replays the fit’s preprocessing and infers per-cell activities against the frozen loadings). The per-cell activity of a coordinated program should recover the planted donor gradient — this is the bridge from donor-level discovery to cell-level readout.

logcounts_sc <- as.matrix(SeuratObject::LayerData(obj[["RNA"]], layer = "data"))
logcounts_sc <- t(logcounts_sc)                   # cells x genes (dense)
proj <- project_programs_to_cells(fit, expression = logcounts_sc,
                                  cell_types = setNames(meta$celltype,
                                                        rownames(meta)))
act <- proj$activity
coord_prog <- grep("^Tcells", colnames(act), value = TRUE)[1]
# Activity is type-specific: cells outside the program's source type get NA,
# so donor means are computed within T cells only.
is_t <- meta$celltype == "Tcells"
donor_mean <- tapply(act[is_t, coord_prog], meta$donor[is_t], mean)
round(cor(donor_mean[donors], a_grad, method = "spearman"), 3)

The high rank correlation between the projected per-cell activity (averaged within donor) and the planted gradient confirms the metacell -> donor fit -> cell projection round trip preserves the biology. Absolute activity levels live on the fit’s scale; the donor ordering is the readout.
